message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"apukeinoksi","gloss":"as/into an aid-means (apu 'help, aid' + keino 'means, device'; translative case)","category":"means/aid","note":"The translator gives a neutral instrument. The sense of drug or medicine, and with it the remedy/poison ambiguity, is not carried over. The verb is 'on keksitty' (has been invented)."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"muistille","gloss":"for memory (allative case of muisti)","note":"Dative of benefit. Earlier in the same speech 'muistiltaan paremmiksi' ('better in their memory') renders mnemonikoteroi."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"viisaudelle","gloss":"for wisdom (allative case of viisaus)","note":""},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"apuneuvoa","gloss":"aid-device, aid-tool (apu 'help, aid' + neuvo 'advice, device'; partitive)","category":"means/aid","note":"The word differs from 274e (apukeinoksi) but shares the apu- ('aid') element and the same neutral sense, so a loose echo remains. It is not the identical word."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"muistille","gloss":"for memory","note":"Identical to the rendering at 274e, so the repetition of memory is kept."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"mieleenpalauttamiselle","gloss":"for the bringing-back-to-mind (mieleen 'to mind' + palauttaminen 'restoring, returning')","note":"A transparent calque meaning 'bringing back to mind'. It contrasts clearly with muisti, though the two share no stem."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"rikkiviisauden","gloss":"of/accusative of 'broken-wisdom', pseudo-wisdom, smart-aleck wisdom (rikki 'broken' + viisaus 'wisdom')","note":"Doxa is not rendered separately; it is folded into the compound rikkiviisaus, 'sham wisdom'. The Greek 'seeming, not truth' is rendered as 'vain rikkiviisauden ... et todellista viisautta' (only sham wisdom, not real wisdom). The explicit idea of 'seeming' or 'reputation' is weakened."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"rikkiviisaiksi","gloss":"into sham-wise ones (translative plural of rikkiviisas)","note":"Same stem as 'rikkiviisauden' at 275a, so the doxa-wisdom link is kept. It is contrasted with 'viisaiksi' (wise)."},"argument":"Both occurrences of pharmakon are rendered as neutral 'aid' words (apukeinoksi, then apuneuvoa). The compounds share the apu- stem but are not identical, and neither carries the medicinal or poisonous sense. Thamus therefore corrects Theuth's claim ('aid to memory' becomes 'aid to reminding') without turning Theuth's own ambivalent word against him, and the remedy/poison pun is lost. The memory/reminding contrast stays clear, and rikkiviisaus/rikkiviisaiksi keeps the echo between the seeming-wisdom passage and the 'wise-seeming' conclusion."}
message.reasoning:
I'm pulling out the precise Finnish wording in the Phaedrus passage: at 274e, "apukeinoksi" is the term for pharmakon (as an aid), paired with "muistille" for memory and "viisaudelle" for wisdom. Then at 275a, Socrates clarifies that what's been invented isn't an aid for memory itself but for "mieleenpalauttaminen" — recollection or reminding.

I also notice "rikkiviisaus" at 275a, a Finnish word meaning something like sham-wisdom or smart-aleck pseudo-wisdom, used to render the idea of false wisdom without a separate word for mere "appearance" (doxa) — the two concepts get merged into one term. The same root reappears later as "rikkiviisaiksi" when describing those who become merely pseudo-wise rather than truly wise, preserving the echo across passages even though the two renderings of pharmakon (apukeinoksi vs. apuneuvoa) use different but related "apu-" (aid) compounds.
